original_question: Let G = (V, E, omega) be a weighted graph with landmark and witness sets L, W subseteq V, and let Dow_alpha(W, L) denote the associated Dowker complex filtration. If G' = (V, E, omega') has the same vertices and edges but a different weight function, how can one bound the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams of the Dowker complexes of G and G' in terms of the supremum distance between omega and omega'? Also, if L and L' are both epsilon-nets for G, what conditions on these landmark sets guarantee that Dow_alpha(W, L) and Dow_alpha(W, L') have the same homotopy type?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 1.4(i)-(ii) in Section 1, "The Dowker complex in metric graphs." ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact two-part target of the paper: (i) stability of the persistence diagrams of Dowker complexes when only the edge-weight function is changed on a fixed underlying graph, and (ii) a homotopy-type comparison problem for Dowker complexes built from two landmark sets that are both epsilon-nets of the same graph. It also uses the paper's notation Dow_alpha(W,L) and keeps the witness set fixed in the second part, which matches the official formulation. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
missing_details: The section-wide standing assumptions are missing: throughout Section 1, G is treated as a weighted simple graph, and the construction is made on the finite metric space (V,d_G) induced by the graph's geodesic distance. A stand-alone version should say this explicitly. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Part (i) should make explicit that the same landmark set L and witness set W are used for both G and G'; only the weight function changes from omega to omega' on the common edge set E. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

The bottleneck-distance question concerns the persistence diagrams arising from the filtered Dowker complexes as alpha varies, not just a single Dowker complex at one scale. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

The supremum distance should be identified as the sup norm of the difference of the two weight functions on the common edge set, i.e. sup_{e in E}|omega(e)-omega'(e)|. The paper states this informally as the supremum distance between omega and omega'. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

Part (ii) should state that L and L' are epsilon-nets for G for the same epsilon, with W fixed, and that the comparison is between Dow_alpha(W,L) and Dow_alpha(W,L') at a common scale alpha. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))

The paper does not fix a homology coefficient field/ring or a particular homological degree for the persistence diagrams in Open Problem 1.4, so a faithful rewrite should leave those unspecified rather than adding new restrictions. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
refined_question: Let G=(V,E,omega) be a weighted simple graph whose induced geodesic distance d_G makes V a finite metric space, let W,L subseteq V, and for each alpha>=0 let Dow_alpha^G(W,L) be the Dowker complex on vertex set L consisting of simplices sigma subseteq L for which there exists w in W with d_G(w,l)<=alpha for every l in sigma. Let G'=(V,E,omega') have the same vertex set and edge set as G but a different weight function omega', and let Dow_bullet^G(W,L) and Dow_bullet^{G'}(W,L) denote the corresponding Dowker filtrations. Find a bound, in terms of ||omega-omega'||_infinity := sup_{e in E}|omega(e)-omega'(e)|, for the bottleneck distance between the persistence diagrams associated with these two Dowker filtrations. Furthermore, if L and L' are both epsilon-nets for G (for the same epsilon>=0) and W is fixed, find conditions on the landmark sets ensuring that, for a fixed common scale alpha>=0, the Dowker complexes Dow_alpha^G(W,L) and Dow_alpha^G(W,L') have the same homotopy type. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper faithfully because it reproduces, almost verbatim, both clauses of Open Problem 1.4: the first asks for a bottleneck-distance stability bound under a change of weight function on a fixed graph, and the second asks for conditions on two epsilon-net landmark sets that force the corresponding Dowker complexes to have the same homotopy type. The nearby background and definitions provide the exact hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand-alone: persistence diagrams and bottleneck distance, the Dowker complex construction, the epsilon-net definition, and the section-wide convention that the graph is viewed through its induced geodesic metric. The rewrite therefore sharpens notation and quantifiers without broadening the problem beyond the paper's stated open problem. ([archive.intlpress.com](https://archive.intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/joc/2023/0014/0004/JOC-2023-0014-0004-a008.pdf))
